# Care home policies and procedures: five free checks, then only the gaps

A common mistake with care home policies and procedures is buying a full set before finding out what is wrong with the one you already hold. Our free check reads five of your care home policies and procedures against the regulations, with no card needed. Spend money only where it finds a gap.

Pick the five an inspector is most likely to ask for first, because the free check covers only your first five. Safeguarding, infection prevention and control, medicines, complaints and governance make a sensible start. Each one comes back rated as covered, partly covered or a gap.

This collection shows what the check reads, which regulation stands behind each core policy and what a written policy costs. It is written for registered managers, owners and nominated individuals who have no compliance department. They still need to show an inspector that the whole set hangs together. No two documents should give staff different instructions.

{product-grid}

## What the check reads, and what it hands back

Most managers do not need a new policy file. They need to know what is wrong with the one they hold. That is why the care home policy check sits first.

### Three things it tests

CareStream reads the wording you upload and compares it with the regulations that apply to your service. It then reports on three things.

- Coverage: every applicable regulation is rated covered, partly covered or a gap, and the check names the policy that evidences it.
- Out of date content: references to retired frameworks, pandemic era instructions, superseded law or a template placeholder nobody filled in.
- Consistency: one document gives staff a four hour escalation route and another says same day.

Near duplicates drift apart, and staff follow whichever page they find first. A contradiction matters on the floor as much as on paper.

The Care Quality Commission (CQC) asks five key questions of every service. The check is built around the regulations behind them. [The CQC assessment framework and its five key questions](https://www.cqc.org.uk/guidance-regulation/providers/assessment/assessment-framework) set these out.

![Policy Gap Detection screen showing a coverage score of 44 percent, regulation gaps and four analysis stages](https://www.carestreamai.com/email-previews/policy-gap-detection.png)

Figure: the summary view, with a coverage score, unanswered staff questions and the four analysis stages.

### What the free plan shows and what paid plans add

You get a verdict per regulation, a coverage score and the name of the policy behind each requirement. Every out of date flag shows what changed, what the wording should say now and a link to the source. Contradictions sit side by side. You decide which document wins.

Paid plans add example wording for every gap and more than five policies. They start with Starter at {{price:plan_starter_month}} a month. The {{count:trial_days}} day trial is the point where a card is asked for, and anything you have checked stays in your account when you move up.

![Out of date content screen listing two flagged phrases in a safeguarding policy with the current wording beside each](https://www.carestreamai.com/email-previews/mock-policy-out-of-date.jpg)

Figure: an out of date finding, with the old wording and the current wording beside it.

## Which policy answers which regulation

Managers often ask for a list of mandatory policies. The law works differently. Knowing how helps you judge what to hold.

### What the 2014 Regulations ask for

The Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014 set the fundamental standards for every registered service.

[Regulation 17 is the duty of good governance](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2014/2936/regulation/17). Providers must set up systems and run them well to ensure compliance. The systems must let the registered person assess, monitor and improve quality and safety.

Policies are rarely named, so cqc policies and procedures are best read as written proof of those systems. The Regulations ask for systems, arrangements and records. A written policy shows an inspector what the arrangements are.

Our guide to the [policies the Care Quality Commission expects a care home to hold](https://www.carestreamai.com/blog/policies-required-by-cqc-for-a-care-home) gives the full list.

### The core set, regulation by regulation

Each core policy answers one or more regulations.

- Safeguarding adults: regulation 13, the duty to protect people from abuse and improper treatment.
- Safe care and treatment, medicines, infection prevention and control, incident reporting: regulation 12, which covers medicines and the control of infections.
- Consent and mental capacity: regulation 11, the need for consent.
- Deprivation of liberty: regulation 13, which bars it without lawful authority.
- Care planning and person centred care: regulation 9.
- Dignity and respect: regulation 10.
- Nutrition, hydration and food safety: regulation 14.
- Premises and equipment: regulation 15.
- Safe premises and equipment: regulation 12 also requires them.
- Fire and water safety: we suggest these sit with premises.
- Complaints: regulation 16.
- Duty of candour: regulation 20.
- Safer recruitment, supervision, training and staffing: regulations 18 and 19.
- Governance, quality assurance, records and notifications: regulation 17.

Citing the right regulation is only a start. The policy must also say who does what, when, and where it is recorded.

### Residential and nursing homes

Homes that give bed and personal or nursing care need the widest set of policies for care homes. Everything above applies. In our view nursing homes also need clinical governance and clinical procedure policies.

Both types of home provide the building as well as the care. For that reason we suggest premises, fire and water safety policies.

Providers must have regard to [the infection prevention and control Code of practice](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-health-and-social-care-act-2008-code-of-practice-on-the-prevention-and-control-of-infections-and-related-guidance) when deciding how they meet the regulations. We suggest a named lead and a plan for outbreaks.

Homes supporting people with dementia or a learning disability may need more. Examples are restraint, least restrictive practice and behaviour support. Every policy needs a named owner, a review date and a plain route for staff to ask questions.

### Domiciliary care, supported living and hospices

Personal care is a regulated activity. A service that gives it must register with CQC, as [the CQC guidance on personal care](https://www.cqc.org.uk/guidance-regulation/providers/registration/scope-registration/regulated-activities/personal-care) explains. The same rules apply. Safeguarding, medicines and complaints all stay, as do consent and training.

For an agency the emphasis shifts. It needs:

- a firm lone working policy
- a rule for entering and securing someone's home
- a plan for missed or late visits.

Premises duties are lighter because the service does not run the building. Equipment it supplies must still be safe.

In our view hospices and services giving nursing care should add clinical governance, end of life and palliative care, and controlled drugs. Lone working, evacuation and first aid matter everywhere.

## Buy written policies, with every price shown

If the check shows a gap, or you hold nothing on a subject, you can buy a policy written for your service. The prices below are the live ones.

### Single policies

Singles run from {{price:policy_single_from}} to {{price:policy_single_to}}.

- The four flagships at {{price:policy_safeguarding}}: safeguarding adults, medicines management, mental capacity with the deprivation of liberty safeguards, and health and safety.
- Most clinical, governance and statutory policies at {{price:policy_mid}} or {{price:policy_ipc}}, including infection prevention and control, complaints, duty of candour and consent to care.
- Lighter ones at {{price:policy_light}}, such as COSHH, first aid and lone working.
- The accessible information policy at {{price:policy_single_from}}.

Each is written from your answers and read by a person before it carries your name. Delivery is within two working days of your answers. You receive a dashboard version and a print ready PDF on your own letterhead, with a sign off and version block.

The first year of updates is included, then {{price:policy_renewal_year}} a year per policy.

![Staff Health Screening Policy open in a preview window showing the policy statement and procedure headings](https://www.carestreamai.com/platform-policy-preview.jpg)

Figure: a policy preview, as staff would read it, with letterhead and footers removed.

### Packs

Packs suit a new registration or a full rewrite.

- HR and Workforce is {{price:pack_hr_workforce}}.
- Clinical Care is {{price:pack_clinical}}.
- Health and Safety and Governance and Data are {{price:pack_themed}} each.
- The Statutory Starter Pack is {{price:pack_statutory}} for the twenty policies every registered service is expected to hold.
- The Complete Policy Library is {{price:pack_complete_library}} for all 66.

Policies written together refer to each other correctly and name the same role holders. Need only two or three documents? Singles usually cost less, so add up your gaps from the check before you choose a pack.

A pack makes most sense when your registration is new and no existing document needs keeping. Nothing then has to be reconciled with older wording.

### How a written policy is made

You answer questions on your registered name, address, CQC numbers and role holders. You also say how you run the service. Those answers feed every policy you buy.

Where you gave a fact, the policy states it. Where you did not, it describes the action required. It never claims something your service does not do. Each policy carries the version, owner and sign off details an inspector looks for.

You cannot edit a delivered policy yourself. Changes go through us and are checked again, so the wording you hold is the wording a person approved.

A policy supports your governance. Training, supervision and audit are where staff practice is evidenced.

## Who gets the most from this

### Who this suits

It suits a manager who inherited a policy file and cannot tell how current it is. It suits a provider preparing for registration, and anyone who bought templates and found two of them disagree.

Domiciliary and supported living providers will notice the difference most, because policy advice is usually written for residential homes.

Hold a full, reviewed set already? Run the check as a second opinion and spend nothing more. Hold nothing? A pack gives you one consistent starting set, and no one will ask you to speak to sales first.

![Policies list for a nursing home showing each policy with its section, status, version and a preview button](https://www.carestreamai.com/images/care-policies/1.webp)

Figure: the policy list, where each entry shows its status and version so you can see what is live.

### Why a small service might choose this route

The usual options are template packs, a consultant at a day rate or a large subscription from a compliance publisher. Templates are quick. Consultants bring judgement. Subscriptions bring volume.

What they rarely do is read what you already hold. CareStream starts there, then writes a service specific policy only where a gap shows.

You pay per policy rather than a monthly licence, see the price first and can stop updates whenever you like. We do not promise a rating and we never call a policy compliant.

The aim is a plain comparison of what your documents say and what the regulations require.

- You upload up to five policies and the check reads them against the 2014 Regulations, with no card needed.
- It flags out of date wording and places where two of your documents disagree.
- You buy a written policy only for a gap the check shows, at the price listed above.

The [free policy gap check for up to five policies](https://www.carestreamai.com/policy-gap-detection) costs nothing and does not call any policy compliant.

## Get started with the free check

Create a free account, upload up to five policies and read the results. The [free policy gap check](https://www.carestreamai.com/policy-gap-detection) page lists exactly what is tested.

To keep a whole set current, read our guide to [keeping a full policy set up to date and organised](https://www.carestreamai.com/blog/care-home-policies-the-complete-guide). It covers review cycles and version control.

## The follow up loop (the core scenario mechanism)
- Manager: /training, tab "Adhoc Training Modules & Questions", view "Live policy training". Buttons: "Generate lesson & questions", "Questions only", "Generate answer options".

- Translation: paid plans only, machine translation, hub menus English only. Catalogue 35 default plus 152 reference languages (pricing page says 50+).
- Gap fixes, wording alignment, approval chain, CQC Inspection Evidence Report: Professional and above.
- Staff incentives: Professional and Enterprise, monthly, individual only, manager approval needed.
- "This is me" resident profiles: Professional and above, 11 sections, family answers wait for admin approval.
- Build your own audit: Enterprise only.
- Trial: 14 days, with a card, paid plans.
- Policy reading: only read sessions (time, scroll, "Mark as read").

## Never say (code does not do it)
- A face to face session automatically triggering generated training.
- A lesson pushed automatically to the staff member on a wrong answer (they open it with Learn & retry).
- Escalation to the manager when a retry is wrong.
- Mock inspections ("CQC Staff Prep" is the nearest thing, and it is not a mock inspection).
- E-signature, version re-acknowledgement, a formal read and sign register.
- Shared device mode, PIN or phone login, offline mode, rota, leave, staff messaging.
- Incident register, complaints register, tasks, care notes, integrations, a public API, deputy cover, access groups, "bank staff" category.
- A family portal (the family page is a demo form). Care plan links.
- Role based assignment of ad hoc training.
- Choosing a specific policy or section for generation.

## Open points to settle with Len before scenarios use them
1. Follow up lesson cache key is source plus question id plus language, with no tenant or module. Possible wrong lesson served across modules or homes. Needs a code check.
2. Follow up generation has no token check, so it is not capped by the monthly allowance.
3. Training Matrix is ungated in code but the pricing page says Professional and above. Supervisions are Enterprise only in code, all plans on the pricing page. Group Benchmarking is Enterprise on the pricing page, not gated in code.
4. Whether FREE_TIER_ENABLED is on in production.
5. Live audit count (103 in code, 105 in notes). Settings count (11 in code, 22 in notes).
6. Whether the "This is me" SQL has been run and the retention cron scheduled; whether the incentives cron is live (the SQL line is commented out).
7. Whether WhatsApp is live for customers and whether the Android app is published.
8. How a manager gets a follow up after a face to face session in practice (a manual allocation of the ad hoc module, which the manager does).

# Ad hoc training and the follow up after wrong answers

Verified from code only, worktree ~/Care_Stream-wt-collprev (apps/api = Express + Prisma, apps/web = Next.js). Nothing was run or edited. Tags: VERIFIED (with path) or UNCERTAIN. Paths below are relative to apps/api/src unless they start with apps/web.

## Headline summary

- "Ad hoc" in the product is a name for the tenant's own "Adhoc Training Modules & Questions" (modules where source is not ai_generated). It is NOT a separate generation engine and there is no policy / section / role picker. The manager picks a topic-named module; the AI finds the matching passages in the home's own policies automatically.
- The follow up after a wrong answer is partly automatic and partly pull. Automatic: the wrong answer immediately appears in the staff member's hub "Follow-up" tab and one debounced email is sent. NOT automatic: the micro lesson itself is generated only when the staff member opens "Learn & retry" (on demand, then cached). It is not pushed, not emailed as a lesson, and not sent as questions.
- The follow up is a lesson (why, key points, scenario) followed by ONE fresh multiple choice check question. It is not a set of follow up questions.

---

## 1. How a manager creates and allocates ad hoc training

**1.1 Screen and labels. VERIFIED.**
- Manager route /training (apps/web/src/app/(admin)/training/page.tsx). Tab label: "Adhoc Training Modules & Questions" (line ~2341, key `modules`). Other tabs: Compliance, Question History, "Schedule Training Questions Delivery", Staff Progress, Face-to-face Training, Training Matrix.
- Inside the tab, a toggle: "Live policy training" / "Live pre-built training" / "Archived" (page.tsx ~line 725). Helper text for the first: "Your own training modules — generated from your uploaded policies (using your AI tokens) and fully editable." The second: "Built by CareStream and ready to assign... these don't use any of your AI tokens."
- The Live list is pre-populated: GET /training/modules calls `ensureAnnualTopicsAsAdhoc` (routes/training.ts ~465-508) which creates an empty, generatable module for every topic in the standard library for the tenant's care setting (source 'manual', frequency 'adhoc', renewal_months null). Topics the tenant has archived are not recreated.

**1.2 Generation buttons. VERIFIED** (page.tsx ~565-600, and the in-page "Button guide").
- "Generate lesson & questions" (blue, "the recommended way"): POST /training/modules/:id/generate-lesson (routes/training.ts ~1526). Builds a sectioned scenario lesson (each section: teach, a care scenario with answer, a quick check) plus a 20 question assessment bank, via `generateAnnualModuleDraft` (services/training/moduleGenerator.ts). Prompt text says 4-6 sections and 20 questions in memory note; code asks for sections with scenario and check and an assessment bank (moduleGenerator.ts ~26). The exact 20 and 4-6 figures come from the memory note only: UNCERTAIN against the editable DB prompt `training_module_generation`.
- "Questions only" (purple): POST /training/modules/:id/generate-questions, up to 20 (default 8) multiple choice questions. Requires a matching TrainingSeed for the module slug, else error NO_SEED (routes/training.ts ~1478).
- "Generate answer options": POST .../generate-answers fills A/B/C/D around question texts the manager typed.
- "Preview" (shows once a lesson exists): steps through lesson and questions read only as staff see it.
- Questions can be edited by hand, "Save changes" (each save is a version in Question History), "Lock questions" (date stamped CQC evidence), "Unlock to edit", archive and restore.

**1.3 Can it be generated from a chosen policy / section / topic? VERIFIED answer: not by policy or section.**
- The manager chooses a module (named by topic, e.g. a statutory or specialist topic). There is no policy picker, section picker or free text topic on this tab.
- The text used: `buildGrounding` (moduleGenerator.ts ~198) runs `homePolicyPassages` (~149), a vector search (embedText + queryVectors in the tenant's own namespace, score above 0.18) for chunks of THIS home's own indexed policies nearest the topic title, up to 6,000 characters, labelled "THIS HOME'S OWN POLICIES (teach these; they take precedence)". It then adds capped reference material: the curated Training Seed for the topic (2,500 chars) and up to 3 anonymised example policies (PolicySeed), labelled as reference "not this home's policy; use only to fill gaps". Total cap 12,000 chars. So: own policies first, but not only own policies. If nothing matches, the prompt says so and falls back on seeds and general UK care good practice (`const grounding = text || 'No specific policy extract...'`).
- The saved module records `policy_refs` (which policies and seeds fed it) so staff can open the source policy and it can be audited (routes/training.ts ~1573).
- Two exceptions where a policy or requirement IS the starting point:
  - Gap detection (Professional+): POST /analytics/gaps/:reference_key/training-module (routes/analytics.ts ~1394) drafts an ad hoc module from a regulation gap's requirements and the points the home is adding to its policies. Checks `has_gap_detection`, costs an AI credit, lands as an UNAPPROVED draft (approved false, frequency 'adhoc', pass mark 80).
  - Induction (not ad hoc): POST /onboarding/generate-questions (routes/onboarding.ts ~71) takes a chosen policy_id (own policy only, first 12,000 chars) and makes 1 to 5 multiple choice questions for a read-the-policy step.
- Mapping to the owner's description: "generated from the company's own policies" is broadly right for "Live policy training" modules. "Pick a policy, section, topic" is NOT supported on the ad hoc tab.

**1.4 Does the manager review or edit before staff see it? VERIFIED.** Generation writes straight onto the tenant's module (questions_version incremented, lock cleared). Nothing is sent to staff until the manager assigns it. The manager can Preview, edit questions, and lock. There is no mandatory approval step for tenant ad hoc modules (the approve/attest/external review flow is for the platform standard library). The gap-derived module is the exception: it is created `approved: false` (routes/analytics.ts ~1431) and "lands in the tenant's training review flow".

**1.5 Cost, credits, limits. VERIFIED.**
- Each generate-lesson / generate-questions / generate-answers call runs `checkAiCreditLimit` (lib/plan-limits.ts ~118): blocks cancelled subscriptions, then `checkAiTokenLimit` (monthly token allowance, lib/ai-tokens.ts), then `checkFreeAiBudget` (Free tier lifetime budget and platform daily cap), then the legacy per action credit limit only if a plan sets one.
- Billed credit rows: `logAiCredit` 'training_lesson' (lesson), 'training_questions' (questions). Per memory notes the per action credit limit is NULL on every shipped plan, so the effective gate is the token allowance (UNCERTAIN on live DB values; code comment lib/plan-limits.ts says "the shipped plans leave it null").
- Token allowances per plan (memory note + apps/web/src/lib/pricing-data.ts "AI tokens"): Starter 6 million, Professional 18 million, Enterprise 30 million per month. Free plan 3 million (apps/api/prisma/sql/2026-11-12_free_tier.sql). Tenants see tokens, but metering is by real cost converted at a reference rate (lib/ai-tokens.ts REFERENCE_USD_PER_MILLION = 1.98).
- No per generation price is shown to the manager; cost to the home is only the share of the monthly token allowance. Assigning a pre-built (platform) module costs no tokens.

**1.6 Allocation. VERIFIED.**
- Two modals:
  - Per module "Assign to specific staff" (components/admin/training/training-modals.tsx `PerModuleAssignModal`): checkbox list of staff (name and job role label), "Select all"/"Clear all", button "Assign to N". It sends NO due date. Also an "assign all" button per module that confirms "Assign ... to all N staff members?" (training page `assignAll`).
  - Top level "Assign Training Modules" modal (`AssignModal`): tick staff (all preselected), tick modules (statutory preselected), optional due date.
- Backend: POST /training/enroll {user_ids, module_ids, due_date} (routes/training.ts ~631). Admin only. Validates that users and modules belong to the tenant, skips existing non expired enrolments, creates `not_started` enrolments. Training only tier tenants cannot free enrol (they allocate purchased licences). Free tenants can assign only published CPD standard courses.
- Roles: there is NO "assign to a role" control on the ad hoc screens. Role based requirements exist separately in the Training Matrix (training_role_requirements, lib/training-matrix.ts) but that reports against roles, it does not auto enrol (UNCERTAIN: memory note says auto enrol by role was a planned next item; grep found no auto enrol for training, only for onboarding new starters in routes/users.ts ~441).
- Scheduling and audiences: "Schedule Training Questions Delivery" rules (routes/training.ts delivery-rules) target audience `all`, `day_shift`, `night_shift` or `specific` staff, on chosen days and time, N questions per send; run by the 15 minute cron `training-delivery` (routes/cron.ts, prisma/migrations/manual_cron_schedules.sql). Also manual send, "return to work" refresher and "post incident" sends exist (routes/training.ts ~1852-2022). These send questions by WhatsApp/email rather than the hub lesson.
- Quota: ad hoc (non ai_generated) modules do NOT count toward the monthly annual training allocation. The allocation counts only source 'ai_generated' non CPD modules (routes/training.ts ~712-716, lib/plan-limits.ts `getAnnualLicenseUsage`). Allocations per month: Starter 10, Professional 30, Enterprise unlimited (pricing-data.ts; Free 0).
- Deadline: optional due date only on the top level modal (`due_date`), plus per module on the Annual page (apps/web/src/app/(admin)/training/annual/page.tsx ~509). The per module ad hoc modal has no deadline.

---

## 2. How staff receive and complete it in the Staff Hub

**2.1 Notification. VERIFIED.**
- On assignment the manager is emailed a summary (notifyAdmin, 'training_updates') and each newly assigned staff member gets an email "New training assigned to you" with a button to the hub: ad hoc goes to /chat?view=training, annual to /chat?view=annual (lib/notify.ts `notifyStaffAllocation`, services/email/outbound.ts ~844-880). Gated by the tenant email preference `training_updates` (default true). The email is English only; it is not translated into the staff member's language (UNCERTAIN whether that is intended).
- Optional proactive question: only if tenant setting `question_trigger` is `auto` (default `on_contact`, apps/web settings page ~2058). Then the FIRST question is sent by WhatsApp if the staff member has a phone number, otherwise by email, translated into their first language (services/training/proactive.ts). A PWA push "New training assigned. Tap to start your training in the hub." goes only if something was delivered via WhatsApp or email.
- So push is not sent on plain assignment unless the auto trigger is on. Web push subscription endpoints exist (routes/me.ts ~190).

**2.2 In the hub. VERIFIED.** Hub is apps/web/src/app/(portal)/chat/page.tsx. Nav entries include "My Training", "Annual Training", "Follow-up" (with red count badge), "My Induction", F2F.
- Ad hoc modules that HAVE a lesson play in the same stepped player as annual training (lesson steps with scenario and in lesson check, then assessment, then result and certificate), launched from My Training "Start training"/"Continue" (components/hub/annual-training-view.tsx; GET /me/annual-training/:id, POST .../submit in routes/me.ts; gate relaxed to `ai_generated || moduleHasLesson`, routes/me.ts ~924, ~1045).
- Ad hoc modules with questions only appear in My Training as an inline question list; staff pick an option, submit, see correct/incorrect, then press complete (page.tsx ~2397-2420, POST /training/enrollments/:id/answer and /complete). UNCERTAIN: the legacy /complete route (routes/training.ts ~991) does not check a score or pass mark server side; completion is client driven.
- Question type: multiple choice with four options (A to D) only. Generators produce 4 option MCQs (moduleGenerator.ts normaliseMcq; parseGeneratedQuestions). No free text or true/false in this path.
- Teach then assess: yes for lesson modules (sections, then assessment). Baseline step: for modules with a baseline the learner answers every question before the lesson (annual-training-view.tsx ~759); UNCERTAIN how generally it is switched on.
- Pass mark: module.pass_mark, default 80 (generate path sets 80 for gap modules; `enr.module.pass_mark ?? 80` in routes/me.ts ~1054). Three failed attempts lock the assessment until the learner revisits the lesson (MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3, relearn_required, routes/me.ts ~1049-1070).
- Languages: staff learn in their first language; second language toggle per step/card for staff with a second language (hubContentLang in routes/me.ts; per card toggle in FollowUpView). Pricing page claims 60+ languages in the hub (pricing-data.ts "Languages in the staff hub").
- Time on lesson is tracked (learn_seconds), and feedback/evaluation forms exist for lesson modules (me.ts learn-time and evaluate routes; memory note).
- Pass: enrolment set `complete`, `expires_at` = now + renewal_months (null for ad hoc, so no expiry), certificate_url 'issued' (routes/me.ts ~1072-1085). Admins are emailed a completion email (sendTrainingCompletionEmail). A requires_practical module holds the certificate at 'pending_practical' until a manager signs off the observed assessment (routes/users.ts ~205).

---

## 3. What happens on a wrong answer

**3.1 Is it automatic? VERIFIED: partially.**
- Every answer selection in the hub calls POST /training/enrollments/:id/answer (routes/training.ts ~934; the lesson player calls `saveAnswer` on each pick, annual-training-view.tsx ~311-314). The answer row is stored with is_correct. If wrong, `notifyFollowUp(tenantId, userId)` fires (routes/training.ts ~984). The same hook exists for induction question steps (routes/onboarding.ts ~580).
- Because the lesson player saves on every pick (not only on submit), a pick that is later changed can already have triggered the follow up email. UNCERTAIN how often this matters; the answer is overwritten (upsert) when they change it.
- The gap is "open" for as long as the answer is_correct false. It shows in the staff member's hub Follow-up tab immediately (GET /me/follow-up, routes/me.ts ~605: any wrong training or induction MCQ, with translation).

**3.2 The email. VERIFIED.** `notifyFollowUp` (lib/notify.ts ~90): to the staff member only, debounced to at most once per 24 hours per person (user.last_followup_email_at), honours email preference `training_updates`. Copy: "Your manager has assigned you new follow-up in CareStream", button "Complete my follow-up" to /chat?view=followup (services/email/outbound.ts ~850). The follow up is not manager allocated; the copy says it is. It is English only. Email only, not push, not WhatsApp.
- A weekly nudge too: every Monday the daily knowledge gap job emails each staff member with open gaps "N thing(s) to revisit" with button "Open my Follow-up" (services/knowledge-gaps/digest.ts `sendTenantRefreshers`; job scheduled daily 07:00 via pg_cron in prisma/migrations/manual_cron_schedules.sql, weekly part on Monday UTC). Gated by email preference `knowledge_gap_digest`.

**3.3 What is generated. VERIFIED (lib/remediation.ts).** On the staff member opening a card and choosing "Learn & retry" the hub calls GET /me/follow-up/lesson (routes/me.ts ~663) which runs `getOrCreateLesson`:
- why: 2-3 sentences, warm, no blame, what the correct answer is and why.
- key_points: 3 to 4 plain language points.
- scenario: situation (2-4 sentences, resident first name), prompt, answer, grounded in the policy.
- check: ONE new multiple choice question (four options, correct_option) on the same concept, phrased differently, not the original wording.
- plus policy_id and policy_title so the card shows "Ask about [policy]" which opens policy chat.
- Written in the staff member's language when not English (prompt: "Write ALL text... in {language}").
- Model: callClaude with feature 'remediation', maxTokens 1600, "should finish in under two minutes".
- Grounding: `buildGapContext`. For training gaps: finds ONE tenant policy whose filename contains up to 4 keywords from the module name (first match, not semantic), reads its extracted text (cut to 6,000 chars); if under 1,500 chars, adds up to 2 PolicySeed entries matching the keywords. For induction gaps it uses the step's linked policy. If no policy text at all, prompt falls back to general UK care good practice. So it is the home's own policy when a filename keyword matches, otherwise reference seeds or general good practice. UNCERTAIN whether the match is reliable for modules whose names do not appear in a policy filename.

**3.4 When, how, to whom. VERIFIED.**
- Generated lazily the first time anyone opens "Learn & retry" for that question and language, not at the moment of the wrong answer.
- Shown in the hub only to that staff member. No email or push carries the lesson. The manager is not notified.

**3.5 Lesson, questions or both? VERIFIED.** Both, but small: a short lesson then a single check question. The alternative "Just retry" re-asks the original question.
- Staff choose per card: "Learn & retry" or "Just retry" (FollowUpView/GapCard, page.tsx ~1978+). After a wrong Just retry the card offers "Learn the point".
- The lesson is stepped: intro, lesson, check ("Check your understanding"). Correct answer clears the gap: POST /me/follow-up/lesson/answer marks the original TrainingAnswer is_correct true (or induction answer_correct), logs a remediation attempt, shows "Correct, well done! This one's now cleared." plus a "Was this helpful?" rating card. Only the correct answer is checked server side; correct option is withheld from the client until answered.

**3.6 What if they get the retry wrong again? VERIFIED.** The card shows "Not quite, the correct answer is highlighted in green. Have another go." with a "Try again" button and "Back to the lesson". Unlimited retries. There is no limit, no lockout, no automatic escalation to the manager. The gap just stays open and counts in the manager's analytics and the weekly digest. Note the 3 attempt cap applies only to the main lesson assessment (routes/me.ts), not to follow up cards.

**3.7 Caching per language. VERIFIED, with a risk.** Stored in `remediation_lessons` keyed `<source>:<ref>` plus lang (apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma `@@unique([ref_key, lang])`). Subsequent staff get the cached lesson. RISK found in code: the key has no tenant id and no module id, and `ref` is the question id. Generated lesson modules use ids `q1`, `q2`... (moduleGenerator.ts ~343) so the same key can collide across modules and across homes. Legacy question modules use random UUIDs and are safe. I did not run it, so whether a wrong lesson is actually served is UNCERTAIN, but the code path allows it (lib/remediation.ts `getOrCreateLesson` looks up by ref_key and lang only). Worth fixing before promising "built from your policies" on every follow up.

**3.8 Cost and gating of remediation. VERIFIED.** `trackAiAction(tenantId, 'remediation', ...)` is non billable (no credit consumed). There is no `checkAiCreditLimit` call before generating a remediation lesson (grep found none in lib/remediation.ts or the follow-up routes in routes/me.ts), so a home that has used its token allowance still gets follow up lessons, though the cost is still recorded as AI usage. Follow up works for every tier that can answer questions.

---

## 4. What the manager sees afterwards

All UI labels from apps/web/src/app/(admin)/analytics/page.tsx unless stated.
- Analytics tab "Knowledge gaps" (admin only: GET /analytics/knowledge-gaps, requireAdmin, no plan gate in code; routes/analytics.ts ~2794). Section "Knowledge gaps: Where your team is getting questions wrong, across training and induction, and how those gaps are being closed". Stat cards: "Open gaps", "Staff affected", "Closed (30 days)", "Engaged with learning" (share of closed gaps where staff did Learn & retry, `engaged_pct`). Chart "Knowledge gaps over time" (daily snapshot, last 90, table knowledge_gap_snapshots). Cards "Most-missed questions" (top 12 by miss count and staff count), "Weakest topics" (top 8), "How gaps are being closed" (Learn & retry vs Just retry bar, "Recently closed" list of last 10). The tab only renders when there is at least one open gap or one closure (page.tsx ~963). Data built by lib/knowledge-gaps.ts `getKnowledgeGapData`. Note: it counts wrong answers still held; "Closed" is logged remediation attempts (last 300 loaded).
- Analytics tab "Training" also has "Training knowledge gaps" (page.tsx ~1233).
- "Effectiveness of Training" tab (Enterprise, `has_effectiveness`, routes/analytics.ts ~2624): "Gaps resolved" (resolution rate), "Engaged with learning", "Put right (30 days)", "How gaps get closed", "Gaps closed over time" (8 weeks). UNCERTAIN whether the lock text for lower tiers is shown in the UI beyond the UpgradePanel (page.tsx ~1555).
- Weekly digest: "Knowledge gaps this week" email to admins and managers every Monday (services/knowledge-gaps/digest.ts): open gaps with change since last week, staff affected, closed this week, engaged %, top 5 most missed questions, top 5 weakest topics, button "View full knowledge-gap analytics". Skipped if no open gaps and none closed. Preference `knowledge_gap_digest` (Settings, Email preferences). Admin "send now": POST /settings/knowledge-gap-digest/send (routes/settings.ts ~458).
- Per person: staff record /staff/[id] (apps/web/src/app/(admin)/staff/[id]/page.tsx): "Recommended follow-up" (open gaps, needs follow up), "How gaps get resolved" (Learn & retry vs Just retry with recent list), and "Mark as reviewed" (POST /users/:id/follow-up/review, routes/users.ts ~188) which records a supervision evidence entry (knowledge_gap_reviews) and clears the flag until a new wrong answer. The page text also mentions re-sending outstanding questions, resetting a module (POST /training/enrollments/:id/reset), or assigning targeted training. Data from lib/staff-record.ts ~329-375.
- Evidence for inspectors: Question History tab and locked question versions (date stamped); per person reviewed records; stored certificates; the F2F evidence and certificates (below); CQC Inspection Evidence Report is a Professional gated feature (`has_cqc_report`, pricing-data "CQC evidence pack"). Whether a single export combines knowledge gap closure with the CQC pack is UNCERTAIN.
- Weekly staff and manager training reminders: cron `training-weekly-reminders` every Monday, and `training-renewals` daily at 08:20 (90/30/7 day staff renewal reminders and a manager digest) (routes/cron.ts; manual_cron_schedules.sql).

---

## 5. Related pieces

**Face to face (F2F). VERIFIED** (routes/face-to-face.ts; whole router gated by `has_face_to_face`, Professional and Enterprise).
- Manager logs sessions (topic = a training module, date, deliverer, allocated staff), marks each person attended / absent / allocated and a competency (not_assessed, competent, not_yet_competent) at POST /face-to-face/sessions/:id/attendance.
- "Send digital module" for the session: POST /face-to-face/sessions/:id/assign-module sends the session's linked digital training module (a tenant module, or a published standard module) to chosen staff as a catch up, typically those who missed. It is manual, per session. It refuses to send a module that has no lesson or usable questions. It marks module_assigned_at on the attendance record and emails the staff member the hub link. This is the real link between a face to face session and ad hoc training.
- Evidence upload per session (POST /face-to-face/sessions/:id/evidence, malware scanned, safe types), stored certificates issued as PDF only once marked attended (POST .../certificate), payroll/owed pay indicator, F2F matrix and renewals, "mandatory by role" (PUT /face-to-face/mandatory). Hub has an F2F view. Training month view and payroll email. Reminders are admin triggered, never automatic.
- Observation checklists / practical competency: modules flagged `requires_practical` hold the certificate until the manager records the observed assessment (POST /users/:id/annual-training/:enrollmentId/practical, routes/users.ts ~205; sign off name, date, note). A printable PracticalChecklistSheet appears in the training page. This is for the library modules; whether ad hoc generated modules can be flagged requires_practical: tenant modules copy the flag from the topic (routes/training.ts ~494).
- There is no automatic F2F to ad hoc generation. The owner's phrase "after a face to face session a manager allocates ad hoc training" is achievable via "Send digital module" or normal assigning, but it is manual.

**Training Matrix. VERIFIED** (routes/training-matrix.ts, lib/training-matrix.ts, tab "Training Matrix"): every staff member against the training their job role requires, combining digital requirements, F2F requirements and "safe to work" workforce credentials (Enterprise `has_workforce_compliance`). Statuses in_date, due_soon, expired, overdue, practical_due, in_progress, not_started, missing, none, agency. Also mirrored on the staff record. Pricing page says "Training matrix with renewals and gaps" is Professional and Enterprise only, but I found no `checkFeature` on the matrix route or tab (routes/training-matrix.ts only `requireAdmin`; training page.tsx tab not locked). F2F columns do depend on `has_face_to_face`. UNCERTAIN whether Starter can see the digital part: likely yes in code, contradicting the pricing page.

**Expiry and renewals. VERIFIED.** Ad hoc modules have frequency 'adhoc' and renewal_months null, so completion never expires and no renewal reminders arise from them (routes/training.ts ~496; routes/me.ts ~1075). Renewal reminders and "expired/overdue/renewals due in 30 days" apply to modules with a renewal period (statutory annual and standard modules): daily cron `training-renewals`. Legacy complete route sets expires_at one year only if module.is_annual (routes/training.ts ~1005).

**Certificates. VERIFIED.** Lesson modules: certificate view in the hub (My Training "Certificate" button) after pass. CPD hours block "CPD Certified, X CPD hours" appears only when the platform has set `cpd_accredited` on the module (memory note, annual training item 8). Ad hoc tenant modules are not CPD accredited (accreditation is platform set on the standard library; tenant tailored modules are non accredited derivatives per the memory note). F2F certificates are separate PDFs stored per attendee.

**How ad hoc differs from CPD courses and induction.**
- CPD certified courses: platform standard library (tenant_id null, source ai_generated, tier 'cpd'), fixed content, free and unlimited on every plan including Free, do not use the monthly allocation, certificate with CPD hours when accredited (routes/training.ts ~690-716; lib/plan-limits.ts). Ad hoc: the home's own copy, editable, uses tokens to generate.
- Induction (onboarding flows): flows of read/confirm and question steps with policy_id and policy_section per step, auto enrolled for new starters by job role (routes/users.ts ~441); wrong induction answers also feed the same Follow-up tab and digest.
- Annual (pre-built) vs ad hoc: annual modules source ai_generated; standard library free to assign but counts against the allocation; tenant "tailored" annual modules use RAG over the home's policies. Ad hoc ones are the "Live policy training" view.

---

## 6. Plan and tier gating

| Part | Free | Starter | Professional | Enterprise | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Adhoc Training tab (generate, assign) | Locked in UI (FREE_LOCKED_TABS includes modules); free can assign only CPD courses at the API | Yes, uses tokens | Yes | Yes | training page.tsx ~2150; routes/training.ts ~657 |

## 7. Where the owner's description is wrong, incomplete or different in the code

1. "Manager allocates ad hoc training generated from policies after a face to face session": the generation is never triggered by a F2F session. The F2F router only offers "Send digital module" for the session's linked module, manually. UNCERTAIN whether the owner means that.
2. The manager cannot choose a policy, section, deadline (on the per module modal) or role when creating ad hoc training. The tool picks policies by topic similarity. A deadline exists only on the top level "Assign Training Modules" modal. Roles are not selectable (staff are ticked individually; the delivery rules offer day shift, night shift, all, specific).
3. Own policies only: not exactly. Own policies lead, but curated seeds and anonymised example policies fill gaps and general good practice is the fallback.
4. "The system automatically generates follow up questions / a short lesson and sends it": no push of the lesson. Automatic parts: the wrong answer becomes a Follow-up item and the staff member gets one email (at most daily) telling them to open their hub. The lesson is generated only when they open "Learn & retry". The result is a lesson plus ONE fresh check question, not a set of questions.
5. Staff can skip the lesson and use "Just retry" (same question again). Retries are unlimited; no escalation to the manager.
6. The follow up email wording says "Your manager has assigned you new follow-up", though no manager assigned it; English only.

9. Training Matrix is not plan gated in code although the pricing page says Professional and Enterprise.
10. ## 7. What staff and managers cannot do (do not imply otherwise)

- No PIN login, no phone number login, no shared-device mode, no offline mode (sw.js does not cache).
- Hub menus and buttons are English only; only content (policies, training, questions, answers, My Progress, emails) is translated.

# 03 Policies, regulation coverage and inspection evidence

Source: code read in ~/Care_Stream-wt-collprev (18 Nov 2026). Paths are relative to that repo root. Tags: VERIFIED (path given) or UNCERTAIN.
Plan names: the pricing matrix is apps/web/src/lib/pricing-data.ts (Starter 85, Professional 230, Enterprise 385 pounds a month). Limits are stored on the DB `plans` table, so the code only confirms them via the plan-limits helpers and the pricing file.

## 0. Plans and gating at a glance

- VERIFIED (pricing-data.ts): Starter = up to 25 policies, 1 handbook, 10 staff users, 500 questions a month. Professional and Enterprise = unlimited policies, handbooks and staff, 5,000 questions a month (Professional) and unlimited (Enterprise).
- VERIFIED (pricing-data.ts, groups "Policies and approvals", "Policy gap detection", "CQC wording alignment"): everything below is ticked for Professional and Enterprise only, NOT Starter: adopt a gap fix with tracked changes, role holder names merged into policies, print ready policy with letterhead and sign off, admin approval with full version history, care manager approval step (optional), care manager policies hub, external approval by one off link, approval trail and automatic republish, regulation coverage analysis, what to add with example wording, where to add it by target policy, legal basis and source, applicability by care setting, out of date content detection, cross policy consistency checking, regulation change tracking and alerts, wording aligned to CQC quality statements, person centred rewording, numbered highlighted suggestions, adopt through review and approval.
- VERIFIED (pricing-data.ts): "Document version history" is ticked on all three plans. "Basic analytics" all plans. "Advanced analytics" and "CQC readiness report" Professional and Enterprise.
- VERIFIED (apps/api/src/lib/plan-limits.ts FEATURE_TIER, getPlanFeatures): gap detection, CQC report, advanced analytics and face to face are the Professional gated flags (`has_gap_detection`, `has_cqc_report`, `has_advanced_analytics`, `has_face_to_face`). Custom audits, effectiveness, training impact and workforce compliance are Enterprise.
- VERIFIED (apps/api/prisma/sql/2026-11-12_free_tier.sql, line 72): a hidden "Free" plan row exists (not public, 5 policies, no handbooks, no questions, `has_gap_detection` true, `has_cqc_report` false, 3,000,000 token limit).
- UNCERTAIN: the Starter plan row's actual boolean flags (has_gap_detection etc.) live in the DB, not in code. The pricing file says Starter has no gap detection; code gates on the DB flag.
- VERIFIED (apps/web/src/lib/free-rollout.ts): `FREE_LIVE = true` so the Free plan is shown on public pages. UNCERTAIN: whether the API env `FREE_TIER_ENABLED` is true in production (apps/api/src/lib/free-tier.ts says free signup is inert until it is).

## 1. Policy upload and library

- VERIFIED file types: PDF, DOCX, ODT, TXT only, max 50 MB per file (apps/api/src/middleware/upload.ts ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS, MAX_FILE_SIZE_BYTES). The extractor also accepts markdown (services/rag/extractor.ts) but the upload filter does not.
- VERIFIED document categories (apps/api/src/lib/policy-categories.ts): "Internal policy", "Staff handbook", "CQC Report", "Business continuity", plus custom categories a tenant adds in Settings. Internal policies carry an optional Section (routes/policies.ts UploadSchema).
- VERIFIED upload routes (apps/api/src/routes/policies.ts): single upload `POST /policies`, bulk upload `POST /policies/bulk` (client splits large selections, names derived from filenames), replacement version `POST /policies/:id/version`. Also an inbound email address per tenant, `policies@<slug>.<inbound domain>` (routes/settings.ts line 138). UNCERTAIN: whether the email inbox actually ingests attachments as policies (only the address is shown in the settings response).
- VERIFIED duplicate handling: pre-flight `POST /policies/check` classifies each file as exact_duplicate (SHA-256 hash), name_match or new. There are also content duplicate flags (`/policies/duplicates`, resolve = keep both / replace / discard) and a "similar named" list (routes/policies.ts, lib/policy-dedup).
- VERIFIED versioning: uploading a new version creates a new policy row with version = old + 1, status "processing", and the old one stays active until ingestion swaps them (routes/policies.ts `/:id/version`, with `previous_version_policy_id`). A separate "History" tab lists versions (apps/web/src/app/(admin)/policies/page.tsx tabs: Active Policies, Archived Policies, History, New policies). Edited policies (via gap fixes) get major versions 2.0, 3.0 and so on, with a read only snapshot per publish (services/analytics/policy-adoption.ts publishDocument, policyDocumentVersion).
- VERIFIED minor edits: a typo or proofreading fix can be applied without the approval chain, recorded as a tracked change, applied straight to the published text, and does not reset staff acknowledgements (policy-adoption.ts applyMinorEdit; route `POST /policies/:id/minor-edit`).
- VERIFIED review dates: `PATCH /policies/:id/review` sets last_reviewed_at (defaults to today) and review_interval_days (1 to 3650). The UI offers 6 months, 12 months, 2 years, 3 years (apps/web/src/app/(admin)/gaps/page.tsx REVIEW_INTERVALS). Publishing an edit stamps last_reviewed_at and defaults the interval to 365 days if none set (policy-adoption.ts publishDocument).
- VERIFIED "Policies due for review" red panel on the Policies page with a "Mark reviewed" button and a "Review" link to /gaps (policies/page.tsx; services policiesDueForReview). A policy is due when last reviewed + interval is in the past, and only policies that have a review date recorded can be "due".
- VERIFIED review reminders: one email per admin per review cycle listing all due policies, re-armed when a new review date is recorded; controlled by email preference `policy_review_reminders` (services/policies/review-reminders.ts).
- VERIFIED out of date detection is a separate free scan, section "Out-of-date content" on /gaps (see section 2). Policies that have never had a review date are counted ("no review date recorded") rather than flagged as defects (gaps/page.tsx PolicyHealthSection).
- VERIFIED approval workflow (services/analytics/policy-adoption.ts submitForApproval, managerApprove, externalDecision):
  - Adopted gap fixes become tracked changes on a PolicyDocument draft; the uploaded original is untouched.
  - Admin approves, then if "require care manager approval" is not switched off (default ON, `require_manager_approval !== 'off'`) it goes to status "With care manager" (pending_manager); then if `require_external_approval === 'on'` (default OFF) it goes to "Awaiting external" (pending_external) with a one off emailed link; otherwise it publishes straight away. Status labels: Live, Draft, To review, With care manager, Awaiting external (gaps/page.tsx MSTATUS).
  - External reviewers use an unauthenticated token link and can approve or request changes; a note is required on rejection (routes/policy-review-public.ts). External links expire after 30 days (EXTERNAL_LINK_TTL_DAYS) and can be revoked or reissued.
  - Rejection returns the policy to draft, with optional per change feedback notes from the care manager. Stale approvals trigger reminders (`remindApproval`, `sendStaleApprovalReminders`).
  - Publishing re-indexes the policy so staff Q&A uses the new text; a `content_propagated` flag records whether the re-index landed.
- VERIFIED print ready PDF: `GET /policies/:id/pdf` builds a letterhead PDF with tenant logo and a sign off block (rows: Registered manager, Approved by, Date approved, Next review, Signature), footer "Uncontrolled when printed" (services/policy/policy-pdf.ts). UNCERTAIN: the route has no plan check in code although the pricing matrix lists "Print ready policy with letterhead and sign off" for Professional and up.
- VERIFIED staff reading: staff read policies in the hub; each reading session records seconds spent, scroll percentage, whether they reached the end and whether they pressed "Mark as read" (or "Done" outside a training step) (apps/api/src/routes/me.ts `POST /me/policy/read`, model PolicyReadSession; web (portal)/chat/page.tsx). Admins see per policy reading engagement (`GET /analytics/policy-reading`) and per staff reading on the staff profile.

Also a gap fix can generate a read and confirm onboarding flow for staff ("Turn a gap fix into onboarding", `POST /analytics/gaps/:key/onboarding`, no AI credit) so staff read and acknowledge the updated policy; the exact UI wording of the acknowledgement was not checked.
- VERIFIED staff reading quizzes: `GET /me/policy/:policyId/questions` generates comprehension questions from the policy text at read time (me.ts).

## 2. Policy screening and gap checks

### 2a. Free screening of the first 5 policies
- VERIFIED: constant `FREE_POLICY_LIMIT = 5`; a Free tenant has a LIFETIME allowance of 5 policy places (replacing or versioning a policy does not use another; deleting does not refund; an identical file already counted is free; a policy that never became usable is refunded) (apps/api/src/lib/free-tier.ts claimPolicySlot, releasePolicySlot). Each has: summary, care home context, curated `required_elements` (the checklist a compliant policy must contain), `expected_policy_titles`, `match_terms`, `distinguish_from` (near neighbour regulations that must not be confused, for example Mental Health Act vs Mental Capacity Act), `authority_basis` (statutory vs advisory), `applies_to_settings` and `required_triggers`.
- VERIFIED the set a tenant is assessed against is scoped to their care setting and service profile (`getScopedRegulations`, `regulationAppliesToTenant`, lib/service-triggers.ts). Setting up Settings > service profile and organisation details affects scope. Before the first run the page asks for missing organisation details (Nominated individual, Registered address, CQC provider ID, CQC location ID, default approver or registered manager) and shows a disclaimer ("Before you run the analysis") and an AI token notice ("A full re-run uses AI tokens").

Memory notes say CS-1001 had 74 regulations in scope (the shop references 57 distinct regulations across 65 policies, per the schema comment). Do not publish a count without checking the database. ### 2c. How the coverage check works and what a result looks like
- VERIFIED (services/analytics/regulation-coverage.ts header): two questions per regulation. 1) SUBJECT (Haiku): does any policy's subject IS this regulation (judged on title, opening and best matching passages; the judge reads content, not just names). 2) ELEMENTS (Sonnet): for the matched policy, the WHOLE policy (up to 60,000 characters) is read against the regulation's curated required elements. All met = covered; some missing = partial (with reasons); no policy about it = gap. Only a missing subject produces a "gap".
- VERIFIED element cap: at most 12 curated elements are assessed per regulation (MAX_ELEMENTS), so "11 of 12" can understate a regulation with more curated elements (also in memory note).
- VERIFIED "Covered" needs every element met; partial is common. The /gaps page leads with how many regulations have a policy behind them (memory note; page headline text not re checked in code this session, UNCERTAIN on exact wording).
- VERIFIED page: "Policy Gap Detection" at /gaps, button "Run coverage analysis" / "Re-run analysis", progress "Checked X of Y regulations" with a keep the page open note (progress saves and resumes). Four pipeline steps with status chips: 1 "Regulation coverage", 2 "Out-of-date content", 3 "Cross-policy consistency", 4 "CQC wording" (gaps/page.tsx PIPELINE_STEPS). Nothing is locked; steps can be run in any order.
- VERIFIED gap drill in ("what to add") (services/analytics/gap-detail.ts): each partial or gap regulation opens a split screen: regulation summary and "legal requirement" vs "recommended good practice" label, the evidence policy, a requirement checklist where each requirement is `missing` or `already_covered` (with the policy it is already covered in), example wording for each missing requirement, a placement (`amend` an existing sentence, `add_under_heading`, or `new_section` with a section title), the target policy it should be added to (can differ per requirement), a suggested new policy title when none exists, numbered highlights in the policy preview, and a disclaimer: "Example wording to review, adapt and approve for your service. This is guidance, not legal or compliance advice." At most 8 requirements per regulation (MAX_REQUIREMENTS).
- VERIFIED safeguard: before recommending an addition, each requirement is checked against the whole policy library; if another policy already covers it, the suggestion is suppressed and the covering policy is named; if everything is covered the verdict is corrected to covered (gap-detail.ts header).
- VERIFIED wording rules: suggestions are written in policy voice ("we will", "staff will"), mirror the target policy's voice, and are checked against a platform key terminology glossary so terms like "lasting power of attorney" are not dropped (gap-detail.ts VOICE_RULES, glossary).
- VERIFIED a tenant can ignore or complete suggestions (`POST /analytics/gaps/:key/decision`, "ignored" or "new_section"), turn a gap into a training module (`POST /analytics/gaps/:key/training-module`, costs an AI credit, module is created unapproved), or an onboarding read and confirm flow (no credit).

### 2d. "Gap fixes": AI rewrites and approval
- VERIFIED the example wording and rewrites are AI generated (Claude Sonnet; gap-detail.ts, saf.ts), then the admin chooses "Adopt" per suggestion (editable text before adopting; an adopt with unchanged text is refused). Adopted wording is applied to a draft with highlighted green blocks (labelled "Adopted") and recorded as a tracked change that can be reverted or edited (`/gaps/adopt`, `/gaps/policy-change/:changeId`). Nothing reaches staff until it passes the approval chain in section 1 and is published ("Adopted changes to review" panel on the Policies page, as named in the pre run warning text).
- VERIFIED: the adoption route calls `checkFeature(has_gap_detection)` (analytics.ts `/gaps/adopt`). Pricing says Professional and up. Free plan has the flag in the SQL seed, so code does not exclude Free from adopting.
- VERIFIED out of date fixes are deterministic and need no AI: the lint modal ("Review & fix", wand icon) pre fills old text to the current term from the signal catalogue (policy-lint-signals.ts `superseded_by`).

### 2e. Out of date detection (Step 2)
- VERIFIED (services/analytics/policy-lint.ts, policy-lint-signals.ts): a deterministic scan, zero AI and zero credits ("This runs instantly and uses none of your AI tokens" in the UI). Button "Scan policies" / "Re-scan policies". Signal categories: superseded legislation, superseded bodies, superseded frameworks, time bound (COVID era wording), unfilled placeholders (XXXX, TBC, lorem ipsum, <<...>>, {{...}}, [insert name] style tokens), structure (very little content under about 600 characters; no policy statement, purpose, aim or scope), review currency (overdue or no review date). Severity high, medium, low with a per policy score. Examples in code: CQC Key Lines of Enquiry (replaced by the Single Assessment Framework quality statements), NHS Digital, Public Health England, CRB, 2010 Regulated Activities Regulations (see also verify-policy.ts OUTDATED_TERMS). The catalogue is editable in the platform console and only approved signals are used for tenant scans (schema PolicyLintSignal.approved).
- VERIFIED each finding can be ignored for one policy or for the whole account ("Undo" supported) and "Mark as updated" hides the policy until a re scan re flags it (memory note project_carestream_lint_ignore.md; routes `POST /analytics/policy-lint/:policyId/ignore|unignore|resolve|reopen`). Ignores never lapse; mark as updated lapses on content change.

### 2f. Cross policy consistency (Step 3)
- VERIFIED (services/analytics/policy-consistency.ts): groups policies that could contradict (near duplicates that have drifted apart, and policies on the same topic via embeddings), extracts checkable claims with Haiku (timeframes, roles, locations, frequencies, thresholds, escalation, definitions), then detects conflicts. A conflict shows: topic, summary, severity (high, medium, low), the conflicting policies with a verbatim quote each, one reconciled wording to replace the conflicting passage in every policy, a kind (`legal` with what the law requires, or `organisational` where the home chooses), and a verification pass. Conflicts can be resolved or dismissed (`/analytics/consistency/resolve|dismiss`). Cluster size is capped at 14 policies.

### 2g. CQC wording alignment (Step 4)
- VERIFIED (services/analytics/saf.ts, apps/web/src/components/admin/wording-review-modal.tsx): per policy, checks the wording against person centred qualities from the CQC quality statements ("expectation cues"), step 1 assesses each quality with an explicit n/a option, step 2 drafts wording only for what is genuinely missing, preferring to AMEND an existing passage (a verbatim 1 to 3 sentence anchor) in the policy's own voice, otherwise add under a heading or a new section. Suggestions are numbered "W" markers in the split screen and adopted into the draft, then go through approval. Costs AI credits.

Read only and free (never starts an AI run). Every in scope regulation left uncovered is grouped under a suggested policy title taken from the regulation's `expected_policy_titles`. Staleness guards: policies changed since the run, not every scoped regulation analysed, or every regulation a gap across 20 or more policies (a pre fix signature). A dated verdict still shows with a note; only an unbelievable one is hidden. Route `GET /analytics/gaps/missing-policies` has no `checkFeature` call, but it depends on coverage rows that only a gap detection run produces.

- NOT a family portal (see section 6).
- NOT instant delivery for shop policies: written, checked and read by a person; the pack page promises delivery within 2 working days after the buyer completes the short questions.
- UNCERTAIN: translation of policies for staff in the hub exists (policy translations table, getEnglishPolicyHtml) but the accuracy and the paid tier of translation are not covered here. Memory says free tier is English only and translation starts on Starter.

### 1.2 Scoring

- VERIFIED: Score = passes divided by scored questions, as a percentage, per audit and per section. A question counts only if it was asked (its condition met), is scored, and was not answered N/A (api/src/services/audits/insights.ts `scoreRuns`; api/src/lib/audit-questions.ts `outcomeFor`, `isScored`).
- VERIFIED: Yes/No questions: Yes passes. A No can be classified by the auditor as the correct answer (counts as a pass) or a genuine gap (fail); this classification is required before an audit can complete (schema `AuditAnswer.no_compliant`; audit-questions.ts outcomeFor).
- VERIFIED: Number questions fail outside min/max; choice and multi-choice fail if a "fail" option is picked; rating fails below pass_min. Findings, free text, date and unscored choice questions are information only (audit-questions.ts outcomeFor).
- VERIFIED: Every visible question must be answered before an audit can complete ("N questions are still unanswered", routes/audits.ts POST /runs/:id/complete).

The paid AI policy writer, AI audit import and minor-edit are denied.

### 4.3 What each plan adds (pricing page comparison rows)

- Starter and above (VERIFIED, pricing-data.ts): chat, email and voice access; basic analytics; regulatory knowledge base; supervisions and appraisals tracking; document version history; AI recommendations at the end of audits.
- Professional adds (VERIFIED): policy gap detection (regulation coverage, what to add with example wording, where to add it, legal basis, applicability by care setting, out of date content, cross policy consistency, regulation change alerts); CQC wording alignment (5 rows); adopt a gap fix with tracked changes; print ready policy with letterhead; admin and care manager approval, external approval by one off link, approval trail and republish; mandatory training by role; face to face training and matrix; training matrix with renewals and gaps; training generated from a policy update; CQC evidence pack, sign in sheets and certificates; training payroll report PDF and CSV; advanced analytics; CQC readiness report; resident profiles ("This is me"); staff incentives.
- Enterprise adds (VERIFIED): build your own audits; audits linked to training (impact); effectiveness of training; training impact; workforce compliance register (DBS, right to work, registration, references) with credential uploads and expiry alerts; multi site group console and benchmarking; priority support.
- VERIFIED code gates: has_gap_detection, has_cqc_report, has_advanced_analytics, has_face_to_face for Professional; has_custom_audits, has_effectiveness, has_training_impact, has_workforce_compliance for Enterprise; has_audit_recommendations for Starter and up (api/src/lib/plan-limits.ts FEATURE_TIER).
- VERIFIED: Resident profiles and Staff incentives are gated on the same flag as the CQC report, so Professional and Enterprise only (api/src/lib/residents.ts `residentsEnabled` uses has_cqc_report; routes/incentives.ts line 30, 50 and routes/residents.ts line 44 give the error text "Resident profiles are on the Professional and Enterprise plans").
- VERIFIED paid only: AI answers beyond limits (query limit), gap analysis and fixes beyond the Free 5 policies, translation (Starter+), resident profiles, staff incentives, AI action plans and recommendations on audits, AI policy writer, audit AI import.
- VERIFIED: Plan change: "Moving up takes effect immediately and moving down takes effect at your next renewal." (pricing FAQ). If the trial ends without a plan "the account pauses rather than deleting anything" (pricing FAQ). Cancelled subscriptions block features (plan-limits.ts assertNotCancelled).
- UNCERTAIN: "Do you offer a discount for charities? Talk to us" is the only discount wording; no code-level charity price.
- VERIFIED: Account closure from Settings, Danger zone "Delete account" (type DELETE), recoverable by support for 30 days (memory project_carestream_pricing_tiers.md; not re-verified in code).

---

## 5. Other modules a manager might expect

- Incident reporting: NOT FOUND as a module. No incident table in prisma/schema.prisma and no incident route. What exists: an "Accident & Incident Book Audit" template (audits.ts PLATFORM_TEMPLATES) and "Post-incident" targeted training (POST /training/post-incident takes an incident description and pushes questions to staff, routes/training.ts line 1978). There is no incident log, no RIDDOR or CQC notification workflow.
- Complaints: NOT FOUND as a module. A "Complaints lead" named role exists for policies (settings.ts), and resident feedback rounds exist as an audit template ("Resident Feedback Round"), plus a feedback route for product feedback (routes/feedback.ts). No complaints register.
- Rota / shift planning: NOT FOUND. Staff have a `shift_type` (any, day, night) used for training and audit shift prompts (users.ts invite schema). A separate internal sandbox "Care_Rota" project exists (memory) but is not part of this monorepo.
- Tasks: no general task manager. Audit actions ("My actions") and training allocations are the only task-like items. NOT FOUND otherwise.
- Handover, daily care notes, care plans, eMAR: NOT FOUND as modules. Care plan and medication appear only as audit templates and policies.
- Notifications: VERIFIED. Email by SendGrid with per-user preference categories (e.g. "audit_updates") (api/src/lib/notify.ts), web push to installed hub PWA (api/src/lib/push.ts; needs VAPID keys, staff must install and opt in), WhatsApp (api/src/routes/whatsapp.ts, services/whatsapp). SMS: Twilio is referenced in routes/whatsapp.ts and settings.ts; UNCERTAIN whether general SMS exists.
- Reports and exports: VERIFIED CSV: training report CSV with costs (face-to-face manager, `training-report-<period>.csv`), training matrix CSV and print to PDF, analytics language breakdown CSV, incentive campaign CSV, staff CSV import ("Import from CSV") (web files above). VERIFIED PDF: audit report PDF per run; training and programme certificates; CQC evidence pack and sign in sheets (pricing rows, Professional). VERIFIED: "CQC Inspection Evidence Report" feature is Professional (pricing row "CQC evidence pack"; `has_cqc_report`).
- Integrations: NOT FOUND for payroll, rota, care planning, HR or accounting systems (no Xero, Sage, Access or similar code). No public customer API or API keys found (the "api key" match is blog-public only). Webhooks exist only for Stripe, SendGrid inbound, WhatsApp and purchases (inbound to CareStream). Training payroll report is a PDF and CSV export, not a payroll integration. Hello Hattie, CareAssura and others are separate products.
- Staff onboarding: VERIFIED onboarding flows and policy seeds exist (api/src/routes/onboarding*.ts), staff CSV import, new starter auto-enrolment into onboarding flows (users.ts invite schema `new_starter`).
- Supervisions and appraisals tracking with actions: VERIFIED, every plan (schema `StaffSupervision`, `SupervisionAction`; pricing row).
- Resident profiles "This is me": VERIFIED (api/src/routes/residents.ts, tables Resident, ResidentInvite, ResidentContribution; Professional+).
- Staff incentives: VERIFIED monthly points campaigns (api/src/routes/incentives.ts; Professional+).

---

## 6. What a buyer might assume the code does NOT do

- No incident register, complaints register, rota, daily care notes, electronic MAR, care plan authoring, resident or family portal for care delivery (Resident profiles are the "This is me" form only), or invoicing.
- No integrations with payroll, rota, HR, care planning or accounting software, and no public API.
- Audits are not a regulator-submitted record. The audit scores are CareStream's own and the CQC readiness score is a blend of audit scores and policy coverage, not a CQC rating. AI recommendations and gap analysis are guidance, with a disclaimer in the code (api/src/lib/residents.ts / analytics.ts line 301: "They are not legal or compliance advice").
- AI recommendations and AI action plans are not on the Free plan.
- Audits can only be edited heavily on Enterprise; other plans can reword and add 2 questions.
- Custom audit allocation is per staff member by ticking, not by group or role.
- Multi site: separate sites do not share policies, staff or settings (each site is its own tenant). The Benchmarking console is a read-only comparison plus switch. No cross-site policy push or shared staff pool was found.
- Role model is coarse: Admin or Staff (plus Staff + Audits). No fine permissions, no delegated cover. "Deputy cover" is not a feature.
- CPD certificates: Care Certificate, Moving and Handling and Medication certificates wait for a manager observation. A CareStream CPD certificate evidences completion, not competence, and not a regulated qualification.
- CPD is free but English only on the Free plan. Translation starts on Starter.
- Free trial is on paid plans only and takes a card; Free accounts have no trial.
- Staff chat limits are per month per plan (500 or 5,000), separate from AI tokens.
- The token allowance resets on the 1st of each month and is not carried over.
- The group/benchmarking claim as Enterprise only is a pricing position and not enforced in code.
