# 05 Resident photos in "This is me" (built 20 Nov 2026, VERIFIED from code and live test)

Plan: Professional and Enterprise, same as This is me.
- Family and friends add photos through the same private invite link (no login), up to 5 photos per link, each up to 5MB, JPEG, PNG or WebP. Each photo is checked, virus scanned and saved again without location data. Optional caption (140 characters) and "who is in the photo" note.
- A manager can also add photos from the resident record (approved at once) and can approve, edit the caption of, or reject any family photo on the Approvals tab. Nothing is seen by staff until approved. Pending photos count in the Approvals badge.
- Photos are private: shown only through short-lived links to signed in staff of the service, never a public address. Only approved photos of living residents. When a person dies or moves on the photos leave the hub at once; pending ones are deleted; approved files stay in private storage for the retention period, like the written profile, then are deleted with it.
- In the hub (This is me chat), staff ask about a person. A question about photos ("do we have a photo of Tim's wedding?") is answered from the approved CAPTIONS and notes people wrote, matched by meaning (wedding finds married, marriage), and the photos appear as thumbnails under the answer; tap to enlarge. If no caption matches it shows that person's photos and says none is captioned that way. If a question does not name a resident and several have photos, the chat asks who is meant.
- The assistant NEVER looks inside a picture and says it cannot describe what is in one. Photos and captions are not used for the assistant's other answers.
- Revoking an invite stops further uploads. After the family member presses Send the link is spent.
- NOT built: video messages (idea under discussion). Do not mention video.

---
# 06 Video messages and family reminders (built and TESTED LIVE 20 Nov 2026, VERIFIED from code and a real phone test)
Supersedes the "NOT built: video" line above. Video IS live. Plan: Professional and Enterprise (same as This is me).
VIDEO MESSAGES
- A family member or friend opens the same private link and taps "Record a message" (opens the phone camera) or "Choose a video". Up to 60 seconds each, up to 5 videos per link, up to 150MB per upload. The upload shows progress and can resume after a lost signal. The clip is converted so it plays on any phone, tablet or computer, and location and device details are removed. They can add a short title (60 characters) and remove a clip before pressing Send. A consent line sits above the buttons ("only share a message you are happy for the care team to play... a manager checks every video before staff see it, and it is removed if the person moves on"). After Send the link is spent.
- A manager approves or rejects each family video on the Approvals tab (preview first, edit the title, add a note). A manager can also upload a video directly (approved at once). Rejected files are deleted at once. Approved videos from family also appear on the resident's From family tab under the person who sent them.
- Hub: in the This is me chat, a question about videos or messages (for example "do we have a video of Tim's daughter?") is answered from the approved titles and notes and the videos appear under the answer with the resident's name and ROOM NUMBER, a poster and play button. A "Messages from family" button in the This is me topic lists a person's approved videos newest first (up to 10 shown per resident). Playing opens just the video on a dimmed backdrop. Each play is logged (who and when) and managers see recent plays on the resident record.
- The assistant never watches or describes a video; it only knows the title and who sent it. Videos are private (short-lived links, never a public address), shown only to signed in staff of the service, only for living residents. When someone dies or moves on, videos leave the hub at once; pending ones are deleted; approved ones stay in private storage for the retention period, like the written profile, then are deleted.
FAMILY REMINDERS
- A manager or admin can ask a family contact gently, by email, to add something new: weekly, fortnightly or monthly, on a preferred weekday, with a pause-until date. Default is off. Each reminder carries a fresh private link valid 14 days. Every email has a "Stop these reminders" link. After 3 reminders with no reply the reminders stop and a manager is told. Reminders stop at once when the person dies or moves on. Settings are on the Family tab, one accordion per contact.
- The reminder email says "a few words, a photo or a short video message".
NOT built: video calls, residents recording back, speech to text or summaries of video, downloads for staff, trimming in the browser.

---
# 07 Speech to text and translation of family videos (built 20 Nov 2026; goes live once the owner runs the SQL and adds the AWS permissions) VERIFIED from code
Supersedes "NOT built: speech to text" and any statement that CareStream does not translate video. Plan: Professional and Enterprise.
- When a family video has been processed, the system starts turning the speech into text in the background. A manager can also press "Transcribe and translate" on any video (including ones the manager uploaded). It runs in the UK region (London) of the same cloud as the private storage.
- On the Approvals screen (video card) and on the video row on the resident record, a "What is said" panel shows: a "Machine generated" tag, "Language: <name>", "Original text (<language>)", and, if the language is not English and is supported, "English translation", with an "Edit translation" link (edits record who edited), the line "Machine generated. Check anything important with someone who speaks the language.", and a tick box "Show the English text to staff when this video is played" (off by default; only available when there is English text; staff see it under the video labelled "English translation, machine generated and checked by a manager", and only once the video is approved).
- States the manager may see: working on it, no speech found in this video, could not read the speech, translation not switched on yet (shows the original text when the transcript exists but translation is unavailable), or an unsupported language (original text only, with a message).
- Languages recognised: English (UK and US), Arabic, Bengali, Chinese, French, Gujarati, Hindi, Italian, Polish, Portuguese, Punjabi, Romanian, Spanish, Tamil, Urdu. Welsh is not supported. Translation into English covers the same languages (not every language that can be recognised is guaranteed).
- Only managers and admins see the transcript and translation, unless a manager ticks "show to staff" for that video. The assistant never uses transcripts or translations. They are not used for search or the chat. The words are deleted with the video in every case (rejected, deleted, profile deletion, pending ones when someone moves on). For an approved video of someone who has died or moved on they stay with the video in private storage for the retention period, then are deleted with it.
- The family page consent box has an extra sentence: if they speak in a language other than English the speech is turned into text and translated so a manager can understand it; only the manager sees this unless they choose to share the English text with staff.
- It is NOT subtitles burned into the video, not live, not for staff by default, and it never replaces a person who speaks the language checking anything important. The video itself is not changed. Titles and notes are still what the chat uses to find a video.
# Feature updates since the 18 Nov fact files (verified in the product, 20 Nov 2026)

These override anything older in files 00 to 04.

- Supervisions and appraisals: on Starter, Professional and Enterprise (booking email, a reminder the day before, a recording form for the conductor, agreed actions in the staff member's "My actions"). The credentials register (DBS, right to work, professional registration, references) and training linked to supervisions are Enterprise only.

files.research/scenarios/ROUTINE-BRIEF.md: # Brief: write scenario pages for the nightly routine (draft only) You write the content for TWO CareStream scenario pages a night. A scenario page is a situation led sales and search page: a care manager recognises the situation, sees the honest gap, and sees how CareStream is used step by step, with its limits stated plainly. The page is a JSON file rendered by existing code. Nothing you do publishes anything: a person approves every page in /platform/blog, Scenarios tab. ## Inputs (all in the engine bundle you downloaded) 1. state.json: `scenario_queue` is the list still to write, in order. Take the FIRST TWO whose slug is not already in `scenarios`. Each item has slug, n (use as `order`), title, hook, features, primary and secondary keywords with UK volumes, and `scene` (for the picture). `scenarios_existing` and `scenarios` list the pages that exist, so you do not repeat their stories, headings or keyword. `published_blog_slugs` is the only source for `read_next`. 2. research/features/00-scenario-facts-summary.md, then 01 to 05 in the same folder. Use ONLY what these let you say; file 05 overrides the older ones. The "Never say" list in file 00 is binding. 3. research/scenarios/scenario-types.ts: the Scenario type and the five mock types (training, followup, language, audit, gaps). 4. research/scenarios/models/*.json: three finished pages. Copy their STRUCTURE, length, tone and level of detail. Never copy their sentences or story. face-to-face-training-follow-up is the follow up loop model; audit-finding-to-action-to-recheck is an audit model; supervision-evidence-of-competence-conversations is a people model. Choose the mock types that fit YOUR scenario: an audit scenario uses audit mocks, a training one uses training or followup, and gaps fits any measuring story. Mock content is illustration only, realistic and not legal or clinical advice. 5. guidelines/00-house-style.md (and product-facts.json if present) for house style. ## The JSON (keys exactly as the models) slug, status "draft", order = n, title (H1 with the primary keyword, then an accent on the last clause), meta_title (under 62 characters, ending " | CareStreamAI"), meta_description (under 156), eyebrow "Scenario", lede (2 or 3 sentences, primary keyword in the first 100 words, one link anchor), fine "14 day free trial · Set up in a day · UK data residency", panel (4 rows, meter 50, pill "Illustration"), image, image_alt, card_title (under 80), card_snippet (under 200; written for someone who has never heard of CareStream), primary_keyword and secondary_keywords (copied EXACTLY from the queue item), feature_links (3 cards; the first must be href /training-platform titled "Training built from your own policies"), intro (heading, sub exactly "A scenario we see in many care settings.", paragraph of 70 to 110 words), trail (exactly 8 steps: 1 to 3 ok, 4 to 7 gap, 8 end; text up to 110 characters), trail_close, why (3 cards, icon chat|tick|alert), how (heading, sub, 4 blocks each with heading, 3 bullets, 1 or 2 tags with internal hrefs, and one mock), talk (8 exchanges, including one about cost or trying it: 14 day free trial or a free account), limits (3 cards of what the product does NOT do here, candid and specific), read_next (2 or 3 slugs from published_blog_slugs), faqs ({heading, groups:[{group, items:[{q,a}]}]}, at least 2 groups and 6 questions), guide ({heading, lede, sections:[{h3, paragraphs?, checklist?}], note}, at least 2 sections, one checklist of 4). Total 1,900 to 2,500 words across all text fields. ## Picture Make one picture per page: POST https://api.carestreamai.com/routine/content/image with {"topic": , "scene": <the queue item's scene>, "key": <slug>}. Use the returned url as `image`. Write `image_alt` (at least 20 characters) to describe what the scene shows. If the call fails, say so in the report and use no image: the page is then not saved. ## Keywords Use the primary keyword in the title, in the first 100 words, and 3 to 9 times in total. Use every secondary keyword at least once, naturally, never more than 6 times. If a keyword does not fit a sentence, restructure it, never force it. Head terms that belong to a product page are used naturally only. ## Style (hard rules) British English. NO em dashes and NO en dashes anywhere. Plain words, short sentences, a warm and direct voice. No hype. Never write the letters AI (say "machine learning", "our own technology" or just "tokens"), never name an AI vendor or model. Do not name or criticise competitors or training providers. Do not state prices. Never say CareStream is the only free route. Say "care settings" or "care services" for generic statements. Allowed HTML in text fields: <a href>, <em>, <b>, <strong>. Never use: mock inspection, e-signature, offline mode, shared device, incident register, complaints register, deputy cover, family portal, care plan link, fire drill register. Never promise compliance, a rating or an inspection result. Law, regulation or official guidance: state it ONLY if you fetched the primary source in this run (legislation.gov.uk, gov.uk, cqc.org.uk, nice.org.uk, hse.gov.uk, skillsforcare.org.uk, ico.org.uk, england.nhs.uk, nhs.uk, scie.org.uk, alzheimers.org.uk) and it supports exactly what you write; link it inline with descriptive anchor text. At least 2 distinct external source links per page. If a claim cannot be verified, leave it out and list it as unverified. Internal links: at least 8 distinct, all real pages (curl https://www.carestreamai.com/sitemap.xml and use only URLs in it, plus /scenarios and /register and /demo), for example /training-platform, /care-audits, /cqc-compliance, /pricing, /how-it-works, /staff-training/<slug>, /uses/<slug> and /blog/<slug> for published blog slugs. ## Saving Write each page to /tmp/<slug>.json, then POST {"scenarios": [ <page> ]} to https://api.carestreamai.com/routine/content/scenarios. The server checks the page (structure, word count, keywords, links, dashes, banned claims). A response with the slug under `created` means saved as a draft. If it is under `skipped`, read the reasons, fix the page and POST again, up to four rounds. If it still fails, do not save it: say why in the report and move to the next queue item. Take further queue items until two are saved or four have been tried. Never save a weak page to reach two.

// Themed groups of six products, for collection pages.
//
// A collection page answers a search phrase, and the six products that answer it rarely
// line up with a bundle: "care home fire safety" wants the fire policy, the evacuation
// policy and the premises policy, which sit across three different packs. So a cluster is
// curated by subject rather than derived from the catalogue.
//
// Six, fixed. It fills two rows of three cleanly at every breakpoint, and a page selling
// four products next to a page selling nine looks like a mistake rather than a choice.
//
// A cluster is reusable across any number of collections: two pages targeting different
// phrases can legitimately sell the same six things, because what differs between them is
// the copy and the search intent, not the products.
//
// Policies and training never mix. The card, the price, the basket and the call to action
// all differ, and a page selling both answers neither search cleanly.

export interface ProductCluster {
  key: string
  label: string
  /** What this cluster is for, shown when choosing one. */
  note: string
  kind: 'policies' | 'training' | 'audits'
  /** Exactly six, in the order they should appear. */
  items: [string, string, string, string, string, string]
}

export function clustersFor(kind: 'policies' | 'training' | 'audits'): ProductCluster[] {
  return ALL_CLUSTERS.filter(c => c.kind === kind)

  return ALL_CLUSTERS.find(c => c.key === key)
}
